categories.main_business_segments: Viking Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing novel therapies for metabolic and endocrine disorders. Its primary business segments are the research and development of small molecule drug candidates targeting diseases such as non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), obesity, X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (X-ALD), type 2 diabetes, and muscle wasting conditions.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core technologies center on orally available, tissue- and receptor-subtype selective small molecule agonists and modulators, including selective thyroid hormone receptor beta (TRß) agonists, dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists, and selective androgen receptor modulators (SARMs). Viking relies on contract manufacturing organizations for production, adhering to cGMP standards, and does not operate its own manufacturing facilities.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Viking’s primary customers will be healthcare providers, hospitals, and specialty clinics treating patients with metabolic and endocrine disorders, pending regulatory approval of its drug candidates. The company targets large and underserved patient populations in NASH, obesity, type 2 diabetes, rare neurological diseases (X-ALD), and muscle wasting following hip fracture.
categories.geographic_coverage: Viking Therapeutics is headquartered in San Diego, California, and operates primarily in the United States, with clinical trials conducted at multiple sites in the U.S. and internationally. The company holds or has filed patents in the U.S., Europe, Asia, and other major global markets, and intends to pursue regulatory approvals and commercialization in North America, Europe, and other key regions.
categories.supply_chain_position: Viking operates as a downstream player in the pharmaceutical supply chain, focusing on late-stage research, clinical development, and eventual commercialization of drug candidates. It outsources manufacturing to third-party contract manufacturers and does not engage in raw material production or active pharmaceutical ingredient synthesis internally.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic focus is on advancing first-in-class or best-in-class therapies for metabolic and endocrine diseases with high unmet medical need. Its R&D priorities include progressing lead candidates (VK2809 for NASH, VK2735 for obesity, VK0214 for X-ALD) through clinical trials, expanding its pipeline in metabolic diseases and anemia, and seeking partnering or licensing opportunities for non-core assets.
categories.revenue_model: Viking currently generates no revenue, as it is a pre-commercial, clinical-stage company. Its future revenue model is expected to be based on product sales of approved drugs, milestone and royalty payments from licensing or partnership agreements, and potentially research funding or grants.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Viking faces competition from large pharmaceutical and biotech companies developing therapies for NASH (e.g., Madrigal, Gilead, Novo Nordisk, Eli Lilly, Pfizer), obesity (Novo Nordisk, Eli Lilly, Amgen, Pfizer), X-ALD (bluebird bio, Minoryx, Poxel), and muscle wasting (Biophytis, Helsinn, Pluri). Many competitors have greater resources and established market presence, but Viking positions itself as an innovator with differentiated, selective small molecule therapies.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2023, Viking had $362.1 million in cash, cash equivalents, and investments, with an accumulated deficit of $377.9 million and no product revenue to date. The company incurred $100.8 million in operating expenses in 2023, reflecting significant investment in R&D and G&A as it advances multiple clinical programs. Viking expects continued operating losses until commercialization or partnering of its drug candidates.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Viking emphasizes the differentiated selectivity and safety profiles of its drug candidates, such as liver-targeted TRß agonists for NASH with minimal cardiovascular effects, and dual GLP-1/GIP agonists for obesity with potential for superior efficacy and tolerability. The company’s pipeline targets large, underserved markets with significant unmet needs, aiming to deliver once-daily oral or convenient injectable therapies with robust efficacy, safety, and combinability with existing treatments.
